arguments.reason: short_irc direction proof WAS computed but cannot be bound to the harness stage because of a Gaussian-log parsing limitation in the machine check. Evidence on disk: calc/irc3.log is a native Gaussian IRC from exactly the submitted TS (calc/ts1.log), both directions converged (141 forward / 39 reverse points, native flag irc_both_directions_converged=TRUE, endpoints -639.003407 Ha RC side / -639.022897 Ha product side). Its reverse outer frame was re-optimized to the RC minimum (calc/endpoint_rev5.log, -639.003420924 Ha, 0 imaginary frequencies, identical to the accepted RC minimum calc/rc2.log) and its forward outer frame to the product minimum (calc/endpoint_fwd5.log, -639.022951022 Ha, 0 imaginary frequencies, C2=C3 1.349 A, C3-Cl4 2.909 A, F1-H5 0.950 A). The same two outer frames were re-extracted and re-optimized independently (calc/endpoint_rev6.log / calc/endpoint_fwd6.log, same energies, max atom deviation 0.0000 A). The harness extractor nevertheless writes endpoint {'filename': null} for every Gaussian IRC log - combined (irc3.log, both flags TRUE) and single-direction (irc4_fwd.log / irc4_rev.log, one side each) - because Gaussian IRC jobs print only 'Input orientation' geometry blocks and no 'Standard orientation' blocks (0 in every IRC log vs 12-34 in the Opt/Freq logs), so it can neither materialise the rx<0/rx>0 outer frames nor pair them with the endpoint Opt/Freq logs; a single-direction log can never expose both sides. The Supervisor independently verified the direction proof in these native files (rev_3b88108a, dec_9fad232c) and stated that the failure is the machine check's input shape, not the science. Disposed as skipped for tool limitation; the IRC connection is preserved in mechanism_graph.json edge e1 (properties.irc_evidence) and in PROCESS.md.

ACCEPT on independent scientific verification of the IRC direction; the remaining short_irc flag is a tooling limitation, not a missing scientific fact.

What I read myself in the native logs (not the workflow flags):
* TS: calc/ts1.log, E -639.002077473, exactly one imaginary frequency -299.6111 cm-1, converged TS optimisation, anti-periplanar geometry (F1-H5 1.355, C2-H5 1.247, C3-Cl4 1.934, C2-C3 1.478 A, D(H-C-C-Cl) 180.0 deg). Mode is essentially pure proton transfer (H5 72.6 %, heavy-atom fraction 0.058, C3-Cl4 projection 0.0045).
* Bidirectional IRC from that TS: calc/irc3.log, normal termination, native irc_both_directions_converged = TRUE, 141 forward / 39 reverse points, summary endpoints -639.022897 and -639.003407.
* Independent single-direction runs from the identical TS geometry: calc/irc4_fwd.log starts at -639.002077 (the TS energy) and reaches -639.022897 after 141 points; calc/irc4_rev.log starts at the same energy and reaches -639.003407 after 39 points. So both directions are reproducible outside the combined job, which removes any doubt that the two branches belong to the same saddle.
* Outer frames re-optimise to true minima: calc/endpoint_fwd5.log -639.022951022 (0 imaginary) and calc/endpoint_fwd6.log the same; calc/endpoint_rev5.log -639.003420924 (0 imaginary) and calc/endpoint_rev6.log the same. The RC-side minimum equals the accepted RC minimum rc2 (-639.003420935) to 1.1e-7 Ha, and the product-side minimum is the accepted sp_1fa042e9 (C2=C3 1.349, C3-Cl4 2.909, F1-H5 0.950 A, no C-Cl or C-F bond). Connectivity therefore changes from the H-bonded complex through a single proton-transfer saddle to the C2H4/HF/Cl- minimum, exactly the declared edge.

Why the machine check still says incomplete, and why that is not chemical doubt: the submitted sidecar irc_endpoints.json for irc3.log declares both endpoints with filename null / sha256 null while recording converged = true on both sides, and the submission API exposes no argument for outer-frame geometry or for the manifest (only ts_file, opt_file, irc_file, irc_forward_file, irc_reverse_file, source_minimum_file, target_minimum_file, reaction_coordinate_description).
